summary:
Inspired by the phases of the moon, Team FishyPhineas has created 'Gibbous', believing that the human body is much alike, wherein gradual changes occur to contribute to a bigger picture in one's overall health. Primarily focused for astronauts, Gibbous is a health monitoring app wherein for 'X' mission days, the astronaut can track their own health telemetries and receive actionable advice by their very own Gibby Buddy. They can choose what files to upload from settings, and visualise it in the app - or even connect devices which send real time telemetries into the app via Bluetooth. 

The 4 main categories are: Biometric Telemetry, Biomarker Registry, Environmental Telemetry and Behavorial Data - all of which simplified and somber for viewing. 
Confused? Click on Gibby Buddy for any analysis or comparison of telemetries.

Any Mission Day data can be viewed once toggled from dashboard. Logs can be made directly from within the app once prior data (Day 0) is recorded. Clicking on any button will open nested graphs. Check below for further functionalities <3
details:
What does it do or how does it work?

  • Acts as a centralized, desktop-based health and telemetry dashboard for astronauts in extreme environments.
  • Ingests physiological and environmental data via Excel/CSV uploads or simulated Bluetooth telemetry.
  • Generates dynamic, visual charts for metrics like HRV, SpO2, bone density, radiation, and sleep architecture.
  • Features "Gibby Buddy," an AI Flight Surgeon that analyzes the uploaded data using the OpenRouter API.
  • The AI returns strict JSON data, which the app parses into color-coded visual blocks (Normal, Caution, Emergency) outlining immediate actions and physiological rationale.
  • Includes a custom visual alarm system that pops up at specific times to remind astronauts to log data.

What benefits does it have?

  • Centralized Monitoring:Replaces fragmented data logging with a unified, high-contrast dashboard.
  • Autonomous Medical Support:Provides instant, medically-grounded feedback without waiting for delayed ground-control communications.
  • Early Anomaly Detection:Compares recent data against NASA guidelines to flag critical issues like hypoxia, bone density loss, or radiation exposure.
  • Routine Enforcement:The visual alarm system ensures critical metrics are logged consistently for mission safety.

What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Safeguards crew health and ensures overall mission success.
  • Bridges the gap between complex raw telemetry and actionable medical advice.
  • Mitigates long-term microgravity health risks through continuous monitoring.
  • Enables rapid, localized response to medical emergencies in space.

What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Language: Dart.
  • Framework: Flutter (compiled for Windows Desktop & Web).
  • Libraries: `fl_chart`, `excel`, `archive`, `xml`, `http`, `file_picker`, `google_fonts`.
  • AI/API:OpenRouter API (utilizing Llama 3 models).
  • Architecture Partner: Claude (used for AI pair-programming, state management, and UI troubleshooting).
  • Data Generation:Python (simulating NASA open science data).
  • Hardware Integrations:Simulated Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) services for live ECG, HRV, and SpO2 sensor connections.

How is your project creative?

  • Immersive UI/UX: Features a sci-fi-inspired aesthetic with a distinct gold/cream color palette designed to look like actual spacecraft equipment.
  • Structured AI Parsing: Instead of returning a wall of text, the AI is forced to return JSON, which the app translates into intuitive, color-coded visual blocks to prevent cognitive overload.
  • Context-Aware Alarms: The visual alarms don't just ring; they explicitly list the specific metrics the user selected during onboarding.

What factors did your team consider?

  • Data Robustness: Built the parsing pipeline to handle missing columns, string-to-double conversions, and format variations without crashing.
  • AI Reliability: Implemented fallback models to ensure the app remains stable if API rate limits are hit.
  • Offline-First: Stored all data locally so the app functions 100% offline, crucial for space missions with limited connectivity.
  • Cognitive Load: Used high-contrast, color-coded UI blocks to prevent sensory overload and enable rapid decision-making under stress.
  • Alarm Precision: Engineered robust timestamp logic to ensure alarms trigger exactly on time without duplicate pop-ups.
  • Privacy: Kept sensitive medical data strictly on the local machine, transmitting it only when the user actively triggers the AI.
